canonical_name: Hickory Nut Gap Farm Barn Dance (Friday Night Barn Dance series)
summary: A monthly ticketed dance night run by Hickory Nut Gap Farm (owned by Jamie and Amy Ager) in their barn in Fairview, featuring a rotating lineup of local bluegrass/old-time/swing/Cajun bands, food trucks, and a bar. The farm intentionally varies the music and dance style (square dance with caller, swing, zydeco) week to week to draw different crowds rather than cultivate a fixed membership, and the event is explicitly sold and marketed as a commercial farm attraction, not a dance club.

evidence.note: All 5 listings share near-identical marketing copy calling it 'our most cherished tradition' framed around farm/fellowship/feasting, with no mention of members, regulars, or a dance community.

Mountain Xpress piece confirms it is farm-run and quotes the farm's marketing lead saying programming is deliberately varied week to week 'to attract different crowds' rather than build a consistent membership base.
Farm sells a paid season pass and per-event tickets through its own shop, i.e. a commercial ticketed product, not a club with membership dues or sign-up.
Farm's own events page lists the barn dance alongside its other farm attractions (fall festivities, etc.), confirming the host organization is the farm business itself, not a dance collective.
